claims.claim: Deterministically archive a verified state and all registered objects; verify one bounded input snapshot offline with exact ZIP, byte identity and canonical replay checks.
limits: Internal integrity does not authenticate reviewers or establish scientific validity.
A valid older history remains acceptable without an externally trusted expected head.
Byte and entry-count limits do not bound general ledger replay CPU complexity.
The initial format is a strict uncompressed ZIP32 subset; it rejects noncanonical repacked ZIP files.

decisions: Keep source changes reviewable in GitHub branches/PRs.
Preserve existing evidence, failure records and frozen source identities.
Do not promote software tests to research checkpoints.
Use one locked _load result and _render output for archive state, without rereading the state path.
Use a strict deterministic ZIP32 format and private computed paths for bounded offline replay.
Publish only after an independent adversarial source review; archive success does not append a ledger event or qualify a checkpoint.
failures: Full baseline with four new adversarial regressions: 52 passed, 4 failed.
A second JSON path read could parse unverified replacement bytes.
A cooperating writer after lock release could make initialize/apply/artifact return the second writer's state.
Archive pre-implementation witness: two missing-module errors and one unsupported export CLI failure identify one absent release capability.
Archive expanded first run: two test fixtures used the wrong note schema; fixtures corrected without ledger changes.
Archive expanded first run: directory fdopen preceded the regular-file check and leaked its descriptor on failure; fstat-before-wrap and unconditional owned-fd closure fixed it.

Archive upper-limit witness: stdlib conservative ZIP64 guard raised an uncaught LargeZipFile; export now reports IntegrityError/CLI exit 2 and preserves cleanup, with the failing 1 MiB scaled probe retained.
